scope: Function contracts and named generated properties. A source-file association is not whole-file verification; direct test imports are not execution coverage.

propertyGroups.formalBoundary: Native IEEE-754 arithmetic, data views, UTF-16 operations and frozen exports remain trusted runtime boundaries.

All supported tree indices, parent/child identities and bounded ragged-tree paths are proved. Native integer guards, exact power lookup and JavaScript execution are calibrated with independent BigInt/binary oracles.
JSON, regex, object descriptors, typed arrays, aliases and chunked async input require native boundary checks.
Mutable maps, WeakRef ownership, deferred finalizers and native byte storage are not established by the pure admission proofs.

Sequential partition, revision, epoch, byte-budget and claim laws are proved. Promise scheduling, failures, callback side effects, rollback and native encrypted-envelope ownership require generated execution histories.
Native signing/encryption and asynchronous delegation verification are outside the proof; integrity checks do not prove cryptographic secrecy or unforgeability.
Third-party CRDT engines, native serialization and out-of-order delivery are outside the proof model.

Scalar order, lexicographic order composition and prefix-page reconstruction are proved within the model. Native IEEE-754/UTF-16 correspondence, field extraction, JSON cursors, index planning and IndexedDB still require independent full-scan and bitwise ordering oracles.
IEEE-754/int32 hashing and bitwise operations are outside the pinned model; generated merge laws and no-false-negative checks do not prove a false-positive probability.
JavaScript object identity, WeakMap ownership, prototype semantics and immutable Redux updates require runtime state histories.
Counter mutation and finite floating-point byte inputs are outside the integer-only functional proof.

Least graph reachability, edge-linear queue bounds and ACL pruning admission are proved for detached nodes and edges. Heap traversal, CID aliases, object snapshots and descendant ACL preservation remain runtime boundaries.

Atomic reservation, exact membership append admission and uint64 epoch sequence laws are proved. Native signature verification, authority lookup, shared mutable budgets, asynchronous queues, callback failures, cancellation, fork latching and byte ownership still require generated execution histories.

Field range/trailer separation and bounded chunk-copy progress are proved. DataView endianness, native safe-integer arithmetic, typed-array offsets, Uint8ArrayList chunks, stream cleanup, canonical decoding and ownership require native malformed-input and model-calibration properties.

Exact first-eligible identity selection, digest multiplicities, strict-majority uniqueness, stable cohort projection and failure precedence are proved. Native bytes and map iteration, authority attribution, reflected probe results, Promise completion order, caller mutation and private error handling require runtime properties. Probe signatures and authorizer correctness remain caller responsibilities.

Production reservation and phase transitions have checked contracts and unbounded finite-history accounting/commit laws requiring both matching context and authorization. Promise cancellation, byte ownership, exact native closure accounting, protected anchor freshness, current-authorization guards, preparation/finalizer contracts and queue isolation remain runtime boundaries. Authentication and causal role authorization are trusted preparation obligations; this is not a whole-document or cryptographic secrecy proof.

integrationBoundaries.boundary: WebRTC/libp2p, NAT/relay behavior, transport loss and browser limits
Real browser storage, restart, eviction and UI scheduling
Packed module loading, API declarations and reference applications
Malformed-input attacks, proxy/getter behavior, cancellation and cryptographic protocol assumptions not covered by a named contract/property

remainingLimits: No whole-product proof or semantic coverage percentage is claimed.
Native cryptographic entropy remains native; generated data and operation schedules have fixed seeds.
The proofs do not establish caller authentication, cryptographic secrecy, durable storage, arbitrary scheduler liveness or browser resource budgets.
Known capability gaps reported by diagnostic scenarios remain gaps.
